author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The death toll from a ferry fire off the Philippine island of Palawan rose to 35 on Friday after rescuers recovered 30 bodies from the burned vessel, authorities said. Firefighters were able to board after extinguishing flames that had blocked access since Wednesday night.

The ferry was carrying more than 130 people when fire swept through it near the end of a voyage to Coron. Reuters reported that 43 people had been rescued as of Friday morning. Officials had previously listed 84 people as missing, but the number still unaccounted for after the latest recoveries was not immediately clear.

Survivor accounts collected by the Maritime Industry Authority described two successive explosions before the blaze. The cause has not been established. The vessel also carried motorcycles, an electric vehicle, a forklift, a pickup truck and other cargo, according to the Coast Guard.

The shipowner said it was cooperating with the government investigation. Search teams continued working through the heavily damaged interior as families waited for confirmed identifications and updated passenger counts. The sharp rise in fatalities is a major development from the initial reports of five deaths.
dek: Rescuers recovered 30 bodies after firefighters entered the burned vessel, while the number still missing remained uncertain.
headline: Philippine ferry fire death toll rises to 35
